To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) RASSF1a is upregulated by the anti-cancer agent Andrographolide in colon cancer and 2) RASSF 1a expression is dependent on the inhibition of angiogenesis signaling.
Andrographolide induces RASSF 1A expression in cancer cells and is associated with suppression of angiogenesis.
Andrographolide induces RASSFIA expression in colon cancer through suppression of angiogenesis and Akt activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying novel molecular targets for the treatment of colon cancer, and to develop novel therapeutic options for the treatment of advanced colon cancer.
the development of new anti-cancer drugs and the identification of new therapeutic targets in colon cancer.
the regulation of tumor suppressors in cancer.

the upregulation of RASFF1A by andrographolides is mediated through suppression of VEGF signaling and activation of Akt in colon cancer cells.
our results demonstrate that RASSF1a expression is regulated by angiogenesis signaling events, and that RASSF 1A expression is suppressed in cancer cells by VEGF.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AGP induces the expression of RASSFA1A and PTENS TSGs in cancer cells by suppressing angiogenesis and Akt activation.
AGP treatment upregulated RASSF1 expression by suppression of angiogenesis and Akt activation, and that this was dependent on VEGF signaling.

The main takeaway from our work is that
RASSF1a expression in colon cancer can be up-regulated with a small molecule drug, Andrographolide, by suppressing angiogenesis signaling.
angiogenesis signaling is a major regulator of RASSFA1A, a TSG that is silenced in many cancers.
RASSF1a and PTEN expression is upregulated by AGP treatment, which is dependent on angiogenic events in colon cancer.
